leading_positions.synthesis: Four of eight members explicitly prefer palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling, all with the same two laureates (Buchwald, Hartwig) and near-identical citation wording. Shared: ligand design made a harsh, substrate-limited reaction general, adoption is long confirmed, and attribution to two names is clean. Not shared: Zou pairs it with a second part for nitrogenase (B003, Rees alone), which the other three do not; Aqvist, Linke and Somfai prefer it alone. All four name the 2010 cross-coupling prize and Kosugi's tin-amide precursor as open points, though all four would credit Kosugi in the narrative rather than the citation. Chabes (rank 6) and Sparr list the 2010 overlap or novelty as a reservation, and Chabes and Sparr would not oppose it as a second choice.

Two members prefer targeted protein degradation, and it has the widest opening ranking (seven of eight members) and is a listed alternative for Aqvist, Linke, Somfai, Sparr and Zou. Shared: a new design principle (small-molecule recruitment of the ubiquitin-proteasome system) that is mechanistically well characterised and general. Not shared: the third laureate. Aili proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa; Chabes proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. Both flag that the PROTAC and cereblon molecular-glue strands may be separate discoveries and that no degrader is yet approved. Brzezinski would treat it as a later-year candidate.

Brzezinski alone prefers long-range electron transfer through proteins (Gray, Winkler), on physical grounding and decades of confirmation. No other member ranks it in round 1; he acknowledges the weak support, the 1992 Marcus prize, and his own field proximity.

Sparr alone prefers biomolecular phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) as a new physical-chemical organising principle. She concedes that physiological relevance is contested and that credit among Pappu, Mittag and Rosen is hard to cut at three; Aili and Linke ranked it sixth at opening and Linke questions its timing.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members consider B011 and B068 to be serious candidates: B011 is preferred by four and is an alternative for Brzezinski; B068 is preferred by two and is an alternative for five others.

Every member who addresses Kosugi would credit him in the scientific background and not as a laureate in a C-N coupling citation, and Buchwald and Hartwig are the only two laureates proposed for B011 in every file that prefers it.
Every member who addresses B068 raises that no PROTAC or degrader drug is yet approved and that the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands may be separate discoveries, so a three-name cut is contested.
No member reports a conflict that would require recusal; several note field proximity only.
Members accept that the committee must state precisely what each candidate adds beyond earlier prizes (2010 cross-coupling, 1992 Marcus, 1980 Sanger, 2023 Medicine mRNA).
scientific_disputes: Whether C-N coupling is a conceptually distinct advance from C-C cross-coupling (different mechanism: amine coordination, deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination, new ligand design; argued by Somfai, Aqvist, Zou, Linke) or a late extension of the 2010 prize (concern raised by Chabes, Sparr, and in the case-against statements of the supporters).
Whether B068 is a new mode of pharmacology (Aili, Chabes) or mostly recruitment of existing ligase biology with bifunctional molecules (Somfai).

Whether the chemistry of B068 is mature without an approved drug: Chabes and Aili hold that the chemistry, not the clinic, must be mature; Aqvist, Brzezinski, Zou and Somfai weigh the missing approval or unsettled citation against it.
Whether nitrogenase (B003) can be honoured on structure alone while the N2-binding site and catalytic cycle remain unresolved (Zou, Brzezinski).
Whether phase separation (B019) is established in cells beyond in vitro behaviour (Sparr, Linke), and whether the field is a chemistry or a physiology topic.
Whether machine-learned interatomic potentials (B001) are stable enough as a field, given the move toward foundation models (Brzezinski, Zou, Linke).
attribution_disputes: B068: Handa (cereblon and molecular glues; Aili, Brzezinski, Linke earlier proposals) versus Ciulli (VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures; Chabes, Aqvist, Somfai, Sparr proposals) for the third place alongside Crews and Deshaies, with Ito, Sakamoto, Gray and Kim left out under any three-name set.
B011: whether Kosugi's tin-amide coupling belongs in the citation or only in the background (Chabes listed him in his opening proposal; the other members in this round would leave him out).
B003: Rees and Einsle as structural anchors against Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe for the biochemistry; Zou's two-part configuration credits Rees alone for the structure part.
B019: experimental discovery (Hyman, Brangwynne) versus theory and sequence grammar (Rosen, Pappu, Mittag).
B001: Behler-Parrinello and Gaussian approximation potential lines are described as separate lineages, with Bartok, von Lilienfeld and E also credited.
B005 (sequencing, discussed in several responses): credit among Balasubramanian, Klenerman, Mayer, Rothberg and Ju is described as contested, as is the effect of the 1980 Sanger prize.
maturity_disputes: B068: no approved degrader; Aili treats this as a possible underweighting by him and Chabes as not decisive, while Brzezinski, Zou, Somfai and Linke treat it as a reason to wait or to settle the citation first.
B011: no maturity concern is raised by any member; the dispute is novelty relative to 2010, not timing.
B019: physiological relevance of condensates is still contested; Sparr herself notes the field is younger than B068, and Linke asks which observations are now beyond dispute.
B003: mechanism not settled, so any citation would rest on structure; Zou and Brzezinski differ on whether that is sufficient.
B001: fast-moving field with attribution still not consolidated; Aqvist concedes it cannot carry a majority this year.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Aqvist: his own field, computational chemistry, is close to B001; he treats it with extra caution and keeps it as an alternative.
Brzezinski: his cytochrome c oxidase electron-transfer work is close to B053, and he is a Stockholm University colleague of Zou; no tie to Gray or Winkler.
Zou: possible bias toward structural candidates (B003, B057) as an electron crystallographer; no known tie to any named candidate.
Chabes: nucleotide metabolism is near B005 and B064 as topics; no personal tie to any shortlisted candidate.
Sparr: lipid and amyloid work is thematically close to B019 and B063; shares Lund University with Linke and Somfai; no recorded collaboration with any listed candidate.
Linke (chair): colleague of Somfai and Sparr at Lund; no stated link to the Buchwald, Hartwig, PROTAC or sequencing candidates. Aili, Somfai and Linke note no specific conflict apparent.
questions_for_round2: Can the supporters of B011 state in one sentence what is new relative to Heck, Negishi and Suzuki, and should the citation name C-N bond formation and ligand design explicitly to keep it separate from the 2010 prize?

For B068, should the committee write one citation covering PROTACs and molecular glues, and if so which three names: Handa or Ciulli beside Crews and Deshaies? Aili and Chabes should say why cereblon or VHL is the more decisive step.
Is the absence of an approved degrader a reason to defer B068, or is maturity of the chemistry sufficient? Brzezinski, Zou, Somfai and Linke should say what evidence would change their view.
Should Kosugi appear in the citation or only in the background narrative for B011, and does anyone present evidence that the tin-amide reaction was closer to the general method than described?
Can Zou's two-part configuration (B011 plus B003, Rees alone) be defended, or would Einsle or Seefeldt have to be added, and would other B011 supporters accept a two-part prize?

What would Brzezinski and Sparr need to see to move from B053 and B019, each ranked first by one member only, toward a candidate that can reach five votes, or would each pair it with another achievement?
Do members who ranked B068 eighth (Brzezinski, Somfai, Sparr) hold that position, and does anyone else regard B063 or B005 as a stronger second choice than B068 or B011?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two leading positions rather than a majority: B011 has four explicit preferences (two-name citation, one member adding a second part) and B068 has two (with different third laureates), while B053 and B019 each have one. The opening rankings were broad for B068 but the round-1 statements moved some support toward B011, including my own first choice from B039. The main open questions are novelty relative to the 2010 prize for B011, and attribution and clinical maturity for B068. Majority is five of eight, so whether B011 can gain a fifth explicit supporter or B068 can settle its citation is what round 2 needs to resolve.
